# Gallivant nonil modules (doc/gallivant/nonil.md): a module whose go.mod
# has a nonil directive is compiled with -nonil, which rejects the
# predeclared identifier nil.

# cmd/go passes -nonil for packages of a main module with the directive,
# and not for the standard library.
go build -n -a -o $devnull ./ok
stderr 'compile.* -p main .*-nonil'
! stderr 'compile.* -p fmt .*-nonil'

go build -o $devnull ./ok
go list -m -json
stdout '"NoNil": true'

! go build -o $devnull ./bad
stderr '^(\./)?bad[/\\]main\.go:6:15: use of nil in nonil module \(use Option, Result or a zero value instead\)$'
stderr '^(\./)?bad[/\\]main\.go:9:12: use of nil in nonil module'

# A module without the directive compiles the same code.
cd plain
go build -o $devnull ./...
go list -m -json
! stdout '"NoNil"'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.27
nonil
-- ok/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"result"
	"strconv"
)

func parse(s string) Result[int] {
	return result.Wrap(strconv.Atoi(s))
}

func main() {
	match parse("12") {
	case Ok(n):
		fmt.Println(n)
	case Err(err):
		fmt.Println(err)
	}
	var p *int // zero values are fine
	_ = p
}
-- bad/main.go --
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var p *int = nil
	fmt.Println(p)
	var err error
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println(err)
	}
}
-- plain/go.mod --
module example.com/plain

go 1.27
-- plain/main.go --
package main

func main() {
	var p *int = nil
	_ = p
}
